title: Ultra — Bletchley Park Intelligence Simulation
description: End-to-end WWII intelligence pipeline decrypting intercepted signals without pre-shared keys and integrating Google Gemini AI for semantic classification. Built with Strategy, Observer, and Factory patterns plus PostgreSQL RBAC isolation.

payload.caption: Cipher Decryption Pipeline & Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) Isolated Routing Tables

deepDive.overview: Inspired by the Allied cryptanalysis headquarters at Bletchley Park during World War II, ULTRA is an end-to-end backend intelligence pipeline that simulates the lifecycle of an intercepted enemy radio transmission. Raw encrypted traffic enters a persistent queue, is cracked automatically without pre-shared keys, is evaluated semantically by an AI triage officer to determine urgency and target command, and is routed strictly on a 'Need-to-Know' basis into compartmented branch databases.
deepDive.architectureSummary: The system follows a decoupled pipeline architecture combining classical OOP design patterns with database-level Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).

pipelineStages.title: Signal Ingestion Queue
pipelineStages.desc: Radio stations push intercepted encrypted payloads and frequency metadata into a PostgreSQL INPUT table.

pipelineStages.title: Factory & Strategy Decryption
pipelineStages.desc: CipherType validates the cipher fail-fast and CipherFactory instantiates the matching keyless cryptanalysis strategy.

pipelineStages.title: Gemini AI Semantic Triage
pipelineStages.desc: Decrypted plaintext is analyzed by Gemini 2.5 Flash to extract target branch (NAVY, RAF, ARMY, PM_OFFICE, SHAEF) and urgency level.

pipelineStages.title: Observer & RBAC Dispatch
pipelineStages.desc: Branch observers persist alerts exclusively to their isolated PostgreSQL tables using least-privilege database roles.

components.name: CipherFactory & CipherType
components.details: Normalizes cipher identifiers into a strongly typed Enum with fail-fast validation and dynamically instantiates the matching DecryptionStrategy.

components.name: Cryptanalysis Engine (decrypt)
components.details: Implements the Strategy pattern across CeaserDecrypt and VigenereCracker so cipher algorithms remain modular and interchangeable.

components.name: GeminiIntelligenceClassifier
components.details: Calls Google Gemini via Java's native HttpClient, parses structured 'BRANCH|URGENCY' results, and falls back safely when needed.

components.name: BranchObserver & PostgreSQL RBAC
components.details: Distributes intelligence via the Observer pattern backed by 6 distinct PostgreSQL roles with granular table permissions.

components.name: UltraPipelineTest Suite
components.details: 9 JUnit 5 & Mockito tests verifying cryptanalysis accuracy, fail-fast factory edge cases, and mocked AI routing.

aiIntegration.overview: ULTRA uses Google Gemini 2.5 Flash to interpret operational military context (such as naval convoy reports vs. air/ground intelligence) and classify urgency.
highlights: Structured Output Parsing: Constrains Gemini to return a clean 'BRANCH|URGENCY' format parsed via ClassificationResult.parse().
Rate-Limit & Retry Handling: Handles HTTP 429 rate limits with exponential backoff.
Zero-Data-Loss Fallback: Falls back deterministically to 'ALL|ROUTINE' if the API key is missing, throttled, or malformed so no intercepted message is lost.

algorithms.name: Caesar Cipher — Chi-Squared Frequency Cryptanalysis
algorithms.explanation: Cracks monoalphabetic shift ciphers blindly without knowing the shift offset by evaluating all 26 rotations against English letter frequencies.
steps: Computes letter frequency distributions for each candidate.
Scores candidates using Chi-Squared against standard English letter frequencies.
Selects the shift with the lowest divergence while preserving original casing and punctuation.

algorithms.name: Vigenère Cipher — Kasiski Examination & Coset Analysis
algorithms.explanation: Cracks polyalphabetic Vigenère ciphers without prior knowledge of the keyword length or letters.
steps: Kasiski Examination: Finds repeated 3-letter trigrams, measures distances between occurrences, and votes on candidate key lengths (2–10) that divide those distances.
Per-Column Frequency Analysis: Splits ciphertext into K interleaved Caesar streams based on the winning key length K.
Recovers each key character by mapping the most frequent letter in each column to 'E'.
